title: Incident-bot: surface related postmortems + open action items (suggest likely causes, link similar incidents)
creator: Miles Thornton
body:
## Context
During recent incidents (e.g., deploy regressions and config push outages), responders repeatedly asked: “has this happened before?” and “what were the follow-ups?” Today that info is scattered across Confluence postmortems, Slack threads, and Linear/Jira action items.

Incident-bot v2 already surfaces first-5-min context (deploy/config/saturation). This ticket adds a lightweight “Related incidents & follow-ups” card to reduce repeat incidents and shorten time-to-mitigation by:
- Linking to prior similar incidents (Slack thread + postmortem)
- Surfacing *open* postmortem action items that match the current incident’s service/symptoms
- Suggesting likely causes (deploy regression vs config change vs capacity/saturation) based on the signals already collected

## Goals
1) **Reduce repeat incidents** by making past learnings and unfinished work visible at triage time.
2) **Improve handoffs** by giving Incident Commander / Oncall a starting point for what to check next.
3) **Keep it safe + bounded**: no tenant/customer data, no expensive queries, and graceful degradation during partial outages.

## Non-goals
- Building a full incident knowledge base / ML-driven root cause analysis.
- Auto-creating postmortems or auto-filing action items.
- Replacing the on-call playbook; this is supplemental context only.

## Proposed UX (Slack)
Add a fourth card (after Deploys / Config diff / Saturation) when enough context is available:

**Card title:** Related incidents & follow-ups

**Sections:**
1) **Likely causes (heuristics)**
   - Example bullets (with confidence indicator text, not a score):
     - “Recent deploy to `gateway` in `us-east-1` within 30m of start → deploy regression is plausible. Check canary + rollback notes.”
     - “Config diff shows routing policy / quota changes in last 60m → misconfig is plausible. Verify propagation + rollback.”
     - “Queue depth + admission control active + GPU util high → saturation is plausible. Consider load shedding / reroute.”
   - Include a disclaimer line: “Suggestions are heuristic; verify with deploy/config/saturation cards.”

2) **Similar incidents (last 180 days, max 3)**
   - For each: `INCIDENT_TITLE` · severity · date · region(s)
   - Links:
     - Slack thread link (if available)
     - Confluence postmortem link (if exists)

3) **Open follow-ups (max 5)**
   - Pull open Linear action items associated with the similar incidents, filtered to the same service (or shared infra like `scheduler`).
   - Render: `KEY` — title — owner — status

**Interactive actions:**
- “Show more similar incidents” (opens modal with paginated list)
- “Copy search query” (copies the query terms used so responders can refine manually)

## Data sources & approach
### Similar incident matching (MVP)
Use a simple deterministic matcher (not embedding search for v1):
- Inputs:
  - Service(s) affected (from deploy card / incident context payload)
  - Region
  - Dominant symptom category (derived from SLO burn / error type / saturation signals)
  - Keywords from incident title if present (from Slack thread opener / incident metadata)
- Candidate corpus:
  - Incident timeline exports (preferred): `slo-toolkit` incident timeline export format
  - Fallback: last N incidents stored by incident-bot itself (thread id, service, region, symptom tags)
- Ranking:
  - Exact service + symptom match first, then service-only, then shared component (scheduler/routing/control-plane)
- Hard bounds:
  - Max 180 days lookback
  - Max 200 candidates scanned
  - Cached results per incident thread for 10 minutes

### Postmortem + action items linking
- For each matched incident, attempt to resolve:
  - Confluence postmortem URL (by stored metadata in incident timeline export OR a maintained mapping table updated during postmortem creation)
  - Linear issue keys tagged as action items (via the postmortem template or manual linkage)
- MVP implementation detail:
  - Maintain a small “postmortem index” JSON blob in an internal store (could be the same service used for deploy metadata export):
    - incident_id, slack_thread_ts, service, regions, symptom_tags, postmortem_url, action_item_keys
  - Index is written by a simple ingestion job (daily) plus a manual backfill script for top incidents.

### Likely cause suggestions (heuristics)
Use existing incident-bot v2 signals and apply rules:
- Deploy regression heuristic:
  - recent deploy within 30–60m AND rollback/canary unhealthy OR error/latency spike aligned with deploy start
- Misconfig heuristic:
  - config diff includes routing policy / feature flags / quota / model pin changes within 60m
- Saturation heuristic:
  - queue depth elevated AND admission control/backpressure active OR KV cache pressure high OR regional capacity warnings

Important: suggestions should *never* display raw config values; only refer to the existence of changes already shown in redacted config diffs.

## Permissions, safety, and audit
- This feature must not expand bot’s access beyond what’s already approved for v2.
- Only display:
  - Confluence postmortem links (already internal)
  - Slack thread links
  - Linear issue keys/titles/owners/status
- Ensure audit logging covers any privileged calls (if any new internal endpoint is introduced).
- If permissions fail or indices are unavailable:
  - Show a degraded card with only manual links (“Search postmortems for service X”, “Open incident timeline dashboard”) and a single-line error reason.

## Acceptance criteria
- Bot renders “Related incidents & follow-ups” card in #incidents threads when service + region are known.
- Shows up to 3 similar incidents within 180 days with at least one working link (Slack or postmortem) per entry.
- Shows up to 5 open action items (Linear) associated with matched incidents.
- Cause suggestions trigger only when supporting signals exist (no empty/hand-wavy suggestions).
- All queries are bounded (time + cardinality) and cached; bot response remains within existing v2 timeouts.
- Feature is behind the incident-bot v2 feature flag and can be disabled independently.
- Security review sign-off for any new data store/index ingestion.

## Implementation notes / tasks (suggested)
- Add a `related_context` section to diag-context payload schema (versioned).
- Build a small indexer job + storage (or extend existing telemetry query service cache) for incident -> postmortem/action-item mapping.
- Implement matcher + ranker.
- Slack card + modal rendering; reuse pagination patterns from large diffs.
- Add metrics:
  - card_render_success
  - index_lookup_latency
  - match_count
  - action_item_count
  - degraded_mode_rate

## Open questions
- Source of truth for incident timeline export in prod: do we standardize on `slo-toolkit` export, or duplicate minimal incident metadata in incident-bot DB?
- Where do we want to store postmortem <-> action item mappings long-term (Confluence macro? Linear relationships? dedicated service)?
- Who owns the ingestion/backfill process (SRE vs Bot team)?
comments: 2025-03-06 (Miles Thornton): This came up again in the Sev1 streaming timeout thread — responders asked for “previous incidents like this” and we spent ~20m hunting. If we can surface even 2–3 prior incidents + their open follow-ups, this will pay for itself quickly. Please keep it bounded; we can’t add heavy queries to the bot during an incident.

2025-03-08 (Jacob Stein): Drafted an MVP that avoids embedding search: deterministic match on service + symptom tags + region, with a small rolling index. Biggest risk is “where do we get the index reliably?” I’m leaning on the slo-toolkit incident timeline export as the canonical feed, with a daily ingestion job + on-demand refresh for the last 24h.

2025-03-10 (Aisha Bello): +1 but please ensure symptom tagging lines up with SLO burn patterns we already use (latency vs 5xx vs streaming disconnects vs saturation). If we invent new categories, we’ll fragment. Happy to review the tag taxonomy.

2025-03-12 (Logan Wright): From a telemetry standpoint: please do NOT do wide queries over incident history at runtime. Precompute and cache. If we can keep lookups to a key-value fetch and a small amount of filtering, we’re good.

2025-03-14 (Naomi Feldman): Security note: linking postmortems and Linear issues is fine, but ensure we don’t accidentally include sensitive snippets from the postmortem body in Slack. Links + titles only for MVP. If you add any new service/API, it needs the same audit events as the config diff work.

2025-03-18 (Dylan Brooks): For Slack: we can reuse the modal pagination component from PR-1854. Suggest we ship this behind a separate flag (`incident_bot_related_context`) so we can disable it if it adds noise during the beta rotation.
status_updates: 2025-03-05: Ticket created out of v2 GA retro; scoped as post-GA improvement.
2025-03-18: MVP approach agreed: deterministic matching + precomputed index, no free-text search in runtime path.
